section_1.title: Prerequisite: Wave-Particle Duality and Superposition
section_1.content: Briefly review the wave nature of light. Explain that light propagates as a wave, and when two waves overlap, they interfere (constructive/destructive). This is the 'foundation' for the complex patterns we will see later.
section_1.example: Visualize two pebbles dropped into a pond; notice how their ripples cross each other to create new, complex patterns.

section_2.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Light Bending Around Obstacles
section_2.content: Define diffraction as the phenomenon where light waves encounter an aperture or obstacle. Introduce the Huygens-Fresnel principle: every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical waves.
section_2.example: An animation showing a laser beam passing through a tiny slit, widening into a pattern of dark and bright fringes instead of just a straight line.

section_3.title: The Core Concept: Interference Patterns as Information
section_3.content: Explain that holography is essentially 'frozen interference.' We record both the amplitude and the phase of the light reflected from an object by interfering it with a reference beam.
section_3.example: A 3D graphical animation showing a reference beam meeting a 'scattered' beam from a toy robot, creating a complex 'interference fringe' map on a recording plate.

section_4.title: Holographic Reconstruction: Decoding the Pattern
section_4.content: Explain the final step: how illuminating the recorded fringe pattern with the original reference beam diffracts the light back into the viewer's eyes to recreate the 3D wavefront of the original object.
section_4.example: A 'magic window' concept: a user moving their head around a hologram of a dragon to see different perspectives, just as if the dragon were physically floating in the air.

section_5.title: Real-World Application: The Future of Data and Imaging
section_5.content: Summarize how these principles extend to medical imaging, security (banknotes), and high-density optical data storage.
section_5.example: Show a smartphone security hologram shifting colors, followed by a quick visual of a futuristic holographic medical display for surgeons.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0) # Per B041

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Columns 4-6 are columns 3, 4, 5 in index-0 based array (offset)
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light propagates as a traveling wave.",
            "Two overlapping waves create interference.",
            "Constructive interference increases wave intensity.",
            "Destructive interference cancels wave amplitude.",
            "This provides the basis for holography."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Wave-Particle Duality and Superposition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup colors
        c1, c2, c3, c4, c5 = "#00FFFF", "#FF00FF", "#FFFF00", "#FF4500", "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        wave1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=c1)
        self.place_at_grid(wave1, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(c1)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
